newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk official says no Iraq oil being pumped.
newsitem.headline: Turk official says no Iraq oil being pumped.

text.p: A Turkish pipeline official said no Iraqi oil was being pumped to Turkey's Ceyhan port on Wednesday because the terminal's tanks had enough crude for a first load.
"No oil has come to Turkey today. It is not needed," an official at the state-run Botas pipeline company told Reuters. "It will probably start when the tanker programme is announced," he said.
He said Iraq had pumped a negligible amount of crude
from Kirkuk on Tuesday but halted the process after a few hours for technical reasons.
Ceyhan has both old crude from six years ago and new oil pumped during recent testing stored in around eight tanks, he said. "There is no difference in the quality between the new and old."
"Three or four (of the tanks) have a mixture," he said. Ceyhan has a total of 12 tanks, each with a capacity of 135,000 cubic metres.
"We are expecting the ship's programme very soon, depending on the U.N.'s approval," he said.
Turkish refiner Tupras said on Wednesday the United Nations had approved its contract to buy 75,000 bpd from Iraq. A ship was on the way to Ceyhan, Tupras said on Tuesday.
